subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On a hot day, a person sweats a lot and becomes dehydrated. How does the body respond to conserve water?
options: More ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb more water
questions.explain: When dehydrated, more ADH is released, making kidney tubules reabsorb more water, producing less, more concentrated urine.

questions.q: A gardener removes the tip of a shoot and the plant stops bending towards light. This is because the shoot tip is where:
options: Auxin is produced, controlling the bending growth response
questions.explain: Auxin is produced at the shoot tip; without it, the unequal growth that causes bending towards light cannot happen.

questions.q: Adrenaline, released in a frightening situation, prepares the body for 'fight or flight' by:
options: Causing the body to fall asleep
Increasing heart rate and boosting glucose supply to muscles
questions.explain: Adrenaline increases heart rate and raises blood glucose, supplying muscles with more oxygen and energy.

questions.q: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration when it rises too high?
questions.explain: Insulin, released by the pancreas, causes cells to take up glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen, lowering blood glucose.

questions.q: How do plant roots respond to gravity?
options: They do not respond to gravity
questions.explain: Roots show positive gravitropism, growing downwards in the direction of gravity, controlled by auxin distribution.

questions.q: A couple are using IVF. FSH and LH may be given to the woman first in order to:
options: Stimulate the maturation and release of several eggs
questions.explain: In IVF, FSH and LH stimulate the ovaries to mature several eggs, which are then collected and fertilised.

questions.q: When blood glucose falls too low, the pancreas releases glucagon, which causes the liver to:
questions.explain: Glucagon makes the liver convert stored glycogen back into glucose, raising blood glucose levels.

questions.q: How does auxin cause a shoot to bend towards light?
options: Auxin destroys cells on the shaded side
Auxin builds up on the lit side, making it grow faster
Auxin stops all growth on the lit side
Auxin builds up on the shaded side, making those cells elongate more
questions.explain: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and increases cell elongation there, bending the shoot towards the light.

questions.q: A plant shoot grows towards light. This response is called:
questions.explain: Growth towards light is positive phototropism, controlled by the hormone auxin.

questions.q: Which is a barrier method of contraception that also helps prevent STIs?
questions.explain: Condoms are a barrier method that physically stop sperm reaching the egg and also reduce STI transmission.

questions.q: Compared with nervous responses, hormonal responses are generally:
questions.explain: Hormonal responses are slower to act but their effects last longer than fast, short-lived nervous responses.

questions.q: What is homeostasis?
options: The breakdown of glucose for energy
The maintenance of a constant internal environment
questions.explain: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, within set limits.

questions.q: Gametes (sex cells) such as sperm and egg are described as haploid because they contain:
options: Twice the normal number of chromosomes
Half the normal number of chromosomes (23 in humans)
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid, carrying a single set of chromosomes (23 in humans) so the full number is restored at fertilisation.

questions.q: Which hormone controls how much water is reabsorbed in the kidney tubules?
questions.explain: ADH increases the permeability of kidney tubules so more water is reabsorbed when the body is dehydrated.

questions.q: Identical twins have the same genes but can still show small differences. These differences are caused by:
questions.explain: Identical twins share the same genotype, so any differences between them are due to environmental factors.

questions.q: DNA is described as a polymer with what overall shape?
questions.explain: DNA is a double helix, two strands twisted together, made of repeating nucleotide units (a polymer).

questions.q: Different versions of the same gene are called:
questions.explain: Alleles are different forms of a gene, for example for eye colour.

questions.q: Urea, which is removed by the kidneys, is produced in the liver from the breakdown of excess:
questions.explain: The liver breaks down excess amino acids in a process called deamination, forming urea that the kidneys excrete.

questions.q: Negative feedback in homeostasis works by:
options: Reinforcing a change so it grows larger
Detecting a change and triggering a response that reverses it back to normal
questions.explain: Negative feedback reverses changes: if a level rises too high, a response lowers it back towards the normal value.

questions.q: What is the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of that organism
questions.explain: The genome is the entire genetic material (all the DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: Which hormone causes the lining of the uterus to thicken during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: Oestrogen, produced by the ovaries, causes the uterus lining to build up ready for a possible pregnancy.

questions.q: A gene is best defined as:
options: A short section of DNA that codes for a protein
questions.explain: A gene is a small section of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a particular protein/characteristic.
